quizName: DMV Practice Test #5 15 Questions • Passing Score 12

questions.question: When another vehicle is passing you, where should you ride?

options.text: In the center of your lane.
On the left side of your lane.
On the right side of your lane.
Move between all three parts of the lane as the vehicle passes.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the center of your lane.
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of your lane when being passed. Riding on the side closest to the passing vehicle increases your risk of a crash. Riding on the far side may cause the other driver to merge back too soon.

questions.question: Which surface gives good traction for motorcycles?

options.text: Wet pavement
Dry pavement
Lane markings
Snow

questions.explanation: Wet pavement, loose gravel, sand, mud, snow, ice, and painted lane markings all reduce traction. Dry pavement provides the best traction for motorcycle tires.

questions.question: How far behind the vehicle in front of you should you ride your motorcycle?

options.text: At least two seconds.
At least three seconds.
At least four seconds.
At least five seconds.

questions.explanation: Keep at least three seconds of distance between your motorcycle and the vehicle ahead. More distance gives you more time to react to other drivers' movements.

questions.question: What does making eye contact with other drivers mean?

options.text: It is the best way to know they see you.
It is not worth your time.
It does not mean they will let you go when they should.
It guarantees they will let you go.

questions.correctAnswerText: It does not mean they will let you go when they should.
questions.explanation: Never assume that a driver who looks at you will yield to you. Drivers often look directly at motorcyclists but do not notice they are there.

questions.question: If a dog is chasing you, what should you do?

options.text: Kick it away.
Stop and wait for it to lose interest.
Swerve around it.
Slow down, then speed up and ride away.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down, then speed up and ride away.
questions.explanation: Dogs are often attracted to motorcycles. Slow down and approach the dog gently. Then speed up and leave it behind.

questions.question: The center of a lane often has an oily strip. Is this safe for motorcycles?

options.text: Never safe.
Usually safe, unless the road is wet.
Usually safe, unless it is sunny.
Always safe, no matter the weather.

questions.correctAnswerText: Usually safe, unless the road is wet.
questions.explanation: Oil from cars collects in the center of traffic lanes. When the road is dry, this area has enough traction for motorcycles. When wet, avoid it. The oily strip is usually only two feet wide, so you can ride around it and stay in the center portion of the lane.

questions.question: What is NOT a penalty for a DUI conviction?

options.text: License suspension.
Installation of a breath-alcohol device on your vehicle.
A fine.
A warning.

questions.explanation: DUI penalties in Illinois include license suspension, required breath-alcohol devices, heavy fines, and community service. A simple warning is not a penalty for DUI.

questions.question: Where should inexperienced riders position themselves in a group?

options.text: At the front of the group.
Right behind the leader.
At the back of the group.
Wherever they are most comfortable.

questions.explanation: Inexperienced riders should ride just behind the leader near the front. This lets experienced riders at the back watch them and help if needed.

questions.question: Why should you turn your head to look over your shoulder before changing lanes?

options.text: Motorcycles have blind spots like other vehicles.
Other drivers will notice you turning your head.
Mirrors are not helpful.
You should make eye contact with surrounding drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Motorcycles have blind spots like other vehicles.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have blind spots you cannot see in your mirrors. Always turn your head to check for vehicles or hazards in your blind spot before changing lanes.

questions.question: How can you be more visible at an intersection?

options.text: Make eye contact with other drivers.
Always ride with your headlight on.
Wave your arms.
Ride close to the vehicle in front of you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always ride with your headlight on.
questions.explanation: Ride with your headlight on and position yourself so oncoming traffic can see you clearly. Keep space around you to avoid hazards. Eye contact alone is not enough to make sure drivers see you.

questions.question: You will ______ hear a tire going flat.

options.text: Always
Usually
Frequently
Seldom

questions.explanation: You will seldom hear a tire go flat. Instead, you will notice the bike handling feels different.

questions.question: In a normal turn:

options.text: The motorcycle and rider should lean together.
The motorcycle and rider should lean in opposite directions.
The motorcycle should lean, but the rider should not.
The rider should lean, but the motorcycle should not.

questions.correctAnswerText: The motorcycle and rider should lean together.
questions.explanation: In a normal turn, the motorcycle and rider lean together at the same angle. In slow, tight turns, only the motorcycle leans while the rider stays upright.

questions.question: The front brake supplies how much of a motorcycle's stopping power?

options.text: About one-quarter
About one-half
About three-quarters
All the stopping power

questions.explanation: The front brake is stronger than the rear brake. It provides about three-quarters of the bike's total stopping power.

questions.question: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield:

options.text: Is not necessary if you have a windshield.
Only protects your eyes.
Helps protect your whole face.
Is less effective than goggles.

questions.explanation: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protects your entire face in a crash. Goggles only protect your eyes. A windshield is not a good substitute for goggles or a face shield.

questions.question: A motorcyclist can discourage other vehicles from lane sharing by:

options.text: Riding in the left portion of a lane.
Riding in the center portion of a lane.
Giving dirty looks if another driver moves into their lane.
Riding in a zigzag pattern to fill up a lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Riding in the center portion of a lane.
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of your lane to discourage other drivers from trying to squeeze in next to you.
